units.title: Overview of the endocrine system
units.summary: Overview of endocrine system • The endocrine system and nervous system are two major parts of human’s coordinating system to integrate activities of all cells and responses to both internal and external changes. Coordinating System Endocrine System Nervous System Affect target cells by Provide sustained Affect target cells by Provide fast Widespread effects Precise effects neurotransmitters responses hormones responses Overview of endocrine system • Endocrine system • A cell (Endocrine gland cell) secretes a chemical. • The chemical (Hormone) travel through the blood. • Another cell (Target cell) is stimulated to change activities.

units.title: Hormone chemical structures and mechanisms of action
units.summary: Hormone Chemical Structure • Chemical structure of a hormone determines its solubility in water. This is related to: • How is it transported in blood? • How does it affect its target cells? • Two classes: • (1) Protein or amino acid based Most hormones are proteins or amino acid based. LH, Epi, ADH) These are usually water soluble and cannot cross cell membrane.

units.title: Regulation of hormone secretion
units.summary: Regulation of Hormone Secretion • The synthesis and release of most hormones are regulated by some type of negative feedback mechanism. • 3 types of stimuli trigger endocrine glands to release more hormones. • (1) Humoral stimuli concentrations of certain molecules (E.g. Calcium ions) in blood • “Low Na + or high K + blood levels ➔ Adrenal gland secretes more aldosterone ➔ Increase Na + and decrease K + • (2) Neural stimuli • “Sympathetic nervous system ➔ Adrenal gland secretes more epinephrine (Epi) ➔ Enhance “Fight-or-flight” responses • (3) Hormonal stimuli concentrations of other hormones in blood Regulation of Hormone Secretion • Pancreas and its endocrine function This is an example of “humoral stimulus”
